meaning: to be in a strong position in a negotiation because one has the advantages that matter most
literal_translation: müzakerede en çok avantaja sahip olmak
example: The government held all the cards in the trade talks, because it controlled access to the only port.
origin: From card games, where a player holding the strongest cards is likely to win; the exact origin of the figurative use is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to play a card game at a party
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This takes the words literally, but the idiom describes advantage in a negotiation, not a game

wrong_meanings.meaning: to show a magic trick using a deck of cards
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with entertainment or illusion

wrong_meanings.meaning: to shuffle papers before an important meeting
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes holding advantages, not organising documents

explanation: 'Hold all the cards' means to have the advantages that will decide an outcome, so the other side has little choice. It is common in political and economic reporting on negotiations.
